authority: owner ruling 'AISEF V2 — CYCLE-2 OWNER REVIEW / P1-P4 ACCEPTED / C2-P5 NOT ACCEPTED / P5 CORRECTION AUTHORIZED / QP-2.6 REMAINS BLOCKED' (2026-09-30)
status: PROPOSAL — NOT APPROVED, NOT APPLIED; no owner approval recorded; LedgerLock not run; QP-2.6 not started

IB-CLI.binding: python -m ledgerlock verify <ledger> | snapshot <ledger> [--out <file>] | apply --batch <file> <ledger> | repair-tail <ledger>, exit codes 0/2/3/4/5

IB-JSONL.binding: the ledger is one JSON object per line with the fields op, key, value (put), ts, id, hash, prev_hash; key NFC; ts an integer; lines newline-terminated
IB-JSONL.source: §3.2, §3.1, §7 (a truncated line is one whose last byte is not a newline)

IB-NAMES.binding: ledgerlock/ledger.py defines Ledger, ConflictError, append, verify, snapshot, apply_batch; a conflicting mutation raises ConflictError

IB-LEDGER.binding: a Ledger is constructed with its ledger file path, Ledger(<path>), and offers apply_batch(ops), snapshot() and verify() as methods; ops are (op, key, value, rid, ts) delivered as 5-element JSON arrays (a contract stimulus is JSON data)
IB-LEDGER.source: §5 names apply_batch(ops) and its tuple shape, §6 snapshot(), §3.4 verify from the library, §12 'the configured ledger path', §13 the class Ledger
IB-LEDGER.gap: the requirements do not say how a Ledger is bound to its path, nor that an implementation must accept arrays where they say tuples; every process_effect spec depends on this binding (the reference and PLAN-V2.1 read it the same way) — open normative gap OG-IB-LEDGER

IB-ELEMENTS.binding: a delete element carries null in its value slot; ts is an integer the caller supplies
IB-ELEMENTS.source: §5 gives every element the shape (op, key, value, rid, ts); §3.2 gives a delete line no value
IB-ELEMENTS.gap: the requirements do not say what a delete's value slot holds

IB-EMPTY.binding: a zero-byte file is a fresh, empty ledger (a valid chain of no lines)
IB-EMPTY.source: §14 item 1 'a fresh ledger'; §3.3 (ok when every line verifies)
IB-EMPTY.gap: a 'fresh ledger' could also be a path that does not exist yet, which §9 makes an I/O error (RISK-4); the specs on an empty ledger (S-5-a, S-6-d, S-7-d, S-9-a, S-9-c, S-9-e) read it as a zero-byte file

decision_3_mappings.criterion: Given the library at this point in the epic chain, when the property test runs 50 random mutation sequences against a temp JSONL (each sequence a list of `(op, key, value, rid, ts)` tuples; seeded with a fixed seed for reproducibility), then for every sequence that did not raise `ConflictError`, `verify()` returns `{"ok": True, "first_bad_index": None}` AND two calls to `snapshot()` return equal dicts.

after.measured: after a fixed conflict-free sequence of mutations (puts, a tombstone, replays, an NFD/NFC replay) the chain the product wrote verifies (`verify` exits 0) and holds exactly the five committed lines

decision_3_mappings.criterion: Given the same property test, when a sequence raises `ConflictError`, the JSONL on disk after the sequence is byte-identical to its pre-sequence state for any prefix up to (and including) the offending element, and the chain length did not grow past that prefix.

after.measured: a sequence whose element conflicts leaves the ledger as the prefix committed it: two lines

decision_3_mappings.criterion: Given the same property test, when it is executed under `python -m unittest discover` and again under `pytest`, both runs report the same total passed/failed counts for the property-test module.
decision_3_mappings.after: unittest/pytest agreement of a test module (DECISION-3; R-11)

decision_3_mappings.criterion: Given the full test suite at this point in the epic chain, `coverage run -m unittest discover && coverage report --include=ledgerlock/*` shows a `ledgerlock/` total line coverage ≥85%.
Given the same full test suite, `pytest` discovers and runs the same suite and reports the same total passed/failed counts as `python -m unittest discover`.
Given the full test suite at this point, the `tests/` source itself is excluded from the coverage measurement.

owner_rulings_applied.OD-D4: applied: 02-02-1 / 02-02-5 rewritten at the requirement level (S-6-a two calls, S-6-d two invocations); the format-module criteria are PLAN_ONLY_DETAIL; no probe added
owner_rulings_applied.OD-GREP: measured: MUST_NOT_HOLD of grep_count {matches: 0} is satisfied exactly when the observation is REFUTED — a count other than 0, OR a non-UTF-8 file (count unestablished) OR an expired window (and a file holding a NUL byte is skipped) — so it expresses 'at least one match' only up to those two causes; not needed: §10/§12 state the prohibitions as absence, so the contracts are MUST_HOLD {matches: 0}, exact
owner_rulings_applied.OD-RETURN: applied: no return shape is prescribed; 'returns the same result' is UNSUPPORTED (R-4.2/2, R-4.4/3)
owner_rulings_applied.OD-REFUSE: applied: refusal is the CLI's exit 5 (§9) and the unchanged file (S-7-e, S-7-f); return-vs-raise is not tested
owner_rulings_applied.OD-BATCH: applied: no batch-file shape is frozen; only the missing-file I/O error is tested (S-9-e); exit 4 and the CLI batch success are UNSUPPORTED
owner_rulings_applied.OD-01-01-6: applied: Ledger and ConflictError are two atomic contracts (S-13-d, S-13-e)
owner_rulings_applied.OD-02-01-4: applied: first_bad_index is UNSUPPORTED (R-3.3/3); no convention promoted
owner_rulings_applied.OD-03-01-5: applied: the crash clause R-5/2 is UNSUPPORTED; no surfacing mechanism is required
owner_rulings_applied.OD-STORE: applied: ledgerlock.store is PLAN_ONLY; its normative content is re-expressed (S-9-d, S-9-a) or UNSUPPORTED
owner_rulings_applied.OD-FACETS: applied: every retained spec observes one clause; multi-clause criteria map to several atomic specs
owner_rulings_applied.OD-STRONGER: applied: no digest value or GENESIS form is asserted (R-3.2/2, R-3.2/4 UNSUPPORTED)

requirement_risks.RISK-1: a key with a committed put can never be deleted or changed (a same-rid delete replays, another rid conflicts): R-6's 'unless tombstoned by a later delete' is unreachable for a put key; tombstones exist only as a first mutation
requirement_risks.RISK-2: R-4.5 'replays of either MUST NOT conflict' holds only for the committed put (S-4.5-b); the refused delete replayed is again another rid (R-4.3)
requirement_risks.RISK-3: replay scope rid alone or rid+key: no spec reuses a rid across keys
requirement_risks.RISK-4: 'verify: any other exit code is a bug' vs 2 and 3; 'fresh ledger' consistent only as an existing empty file (IB-EMPTY)
requirement_risks.RISK-5: 'any modification detected' vs hashing canonical bytes: only semantic edits are testable (S-3.3-* edit value, op, hash, prev_hash)
requirement_risks.RISK-6: the GENESIS form is both 'the literal' and an implementation choice (R-3.2/4 UNSUPPORTED)
requirement_risks.RISK-7: §12 file confinement vs §5's sibling temp file (R-12/2 UNSUPPORTED)
requirement_risks.RISK-9: a newline-terminated corrupt last line is neither truncated nor 'in the middle' (AC-STORY-03-02-4 UNSUPPORTED)
requirement_risks.RISK-10: conflicts and replays between elements of one batch: R-4.3 judges against committed mutations (S-5-a conflicts against a committed line)
requirement_risks.RISK-11: §10's allowed set omits __future__ (which §10 requires) and the package's own modules: S-10-a admits both
requirement_risks.RISK-12: §3.2's line shapes omit hash and prev_hash, which every line carries
requirement_risks.RISK-13: module functions vs methods; append/put/delete signatures and ts provenance open (IB-LEDGER, IB-ELEMENTS)
requirement_risks.RISK-14: durability, crash atomicity, file confinement and the interpreter version are outside every probe
requirement_risks.RISK-15: '0 — success (append …)' names a CLI append no clause specifies
requirement_risks.RISK-16: 'no third-party imports succeed at runtime' reads as an environment property (R-14 item 6 mapped to S-10-a)

clauses.clause: purpose
clauses.reason: descriptive; the behaviours are R-3..R-9

clauses.clause: non-goals (no network listener, database, client/server, third-party deps)
clauses.reason: descriptive; the side-channel half is measured under R-12, the dependency half under R-10

clauses.clause: all keys are normalized to Unicode NFC before storage, lookup, hashing, serialization
strings differing only in NFC/NFD are the same key
a single JSONL file; each line {op, key <nfc>, value, ts <int>, id <rid>}
hash = SHA-256(prev_hash || '|' || canonical_bytes), hash fields emptied
clauses.reason: the canonical bytes encoding is not fixed: no harness can recompute a hash value independently; the product's own consistency is observed through its verify (S-3.2-a, S-3.3-*)

clauses.clause: prev_hash of the next line = this hash
clauses.note: observed through the product's full verify; no observable compares two fields of a file

clauses.clause: first prev_hash is 'GENESIS' or 64 zeros, an implementation choice, documented and constant
clauses.reason: a disjunctive expected value: every file shape compares one value; fixing one form would enforce a stronger property than the requirement (OD-STRONGER)

clauses.clause: append-only: existing records MUST NOT be rewritten in place
a mutated value, swapped op or modified hash on a committed line is detected by a full verify
ok iff every recomputed hash matches AND every prev_hash matches the previous stored hash
ok=False and first_bad_index=<i> on the first violation
clauses.reason: the verdict's representation is open (the CLI exposes the exit code only); no class reads one field of an arbitrary returned object; a fixed-shape comparison would prescribe a representation (OD-02-01-4)

clauses.clause: verify reads no in-memory state set by append; recomputes from disk, CLI or library
a rid is a non-empty UTF-8 string supplied by the caller
clauses.reason: a definition of the caller's input; the requirements prescribe no behaviour for a violation (the reference's refusal of an empty rid is its interpretation)

clauses.clause: a replayed rid MUST NOT append a new line
the second call MUST return the same result
clauses.reason: the result's representation is open; the only comparator of two results needs a JSON form, which would prescribe one (OD-RETURN)

clauses.clause: another rid on a key last mutated by another rid MUST raise ConflictError
... and MUST NOT append a new line
or return an error result depending on CLI surface (exit 4, §9)
clauses.reason: the only mutating CLI invocation is `apply --batch <file>`, whose file shape the requirements do not fix (OD-BATCH)

clauses.clause: a put with another rid after a tombstone MUST conflict
a put with the tombstone's rid is a no-op replay
... returning the same result as the delete
clauses.reason: as R-4.2/2 (OD-RETURN)

clauses.clause: put k r1 then delete k r2: the second MUST conflict
replays of either MUST NOT conflict
apply_batch runs 'under the lock'
clauses.reason: the requirements define no lock and nothing observable depends on one

clauses.clause: apply_batch writes all lines to a sibling temp file, fsyncs it, renames it over the path
clauses.reason: the mechanism is not observable by any class (no step traces the subject's own files)

clauses.clause: a crash at any point leaves the full batch or the pre-batch bytes, never a partial batch
clauses.reason: a fault step makes the faulted call either return (call) or raise (expect_raises); the requirements fix neither, only the post-crash state, and a fault the implementation does not use (os.replace vs os.rename) never fires (OD-03-01-5)

clauses.clause: all or nothing without a crash: a refused batch commits nothing; an accepted one every element
the CLI `apply --batch <file>` performs the same atomic operation
clauses.reason: the batch-file shape is not fixed (OD-BATCH); the file-absent I/O error is measured (S-9-e)

clauses.clause: the snapshot is deterministic, byte-stable for a given chain
the materialised state: each key's most recent committed put unless tombstoned
clauses.note: measured relationally (a refused delete and a tombstone leave the state unchanged)

clauses.clause: sorted by NFC key in UTF-8 byte order; a JSON document
clauses.reason: the document's layout and representation are open: its content and key order are observable only through bytes or a representation no requirement fixes

clauses.clause: the CLI `snapshot --out <file>` writes this same document
clauses.reason: no class compares a written file with a library value, and the file's bytes are layout-open

clauses.clause: a truncated final line is removed and the chain verifies cleanly afterwards
no other content may be modified
clauses.reason: the preserved lines were written by the product: their bytes are unknown to the harness (S-7-a measures that they remain)

clauses.clause: on a clean chain repair-tail is a no-op
on mid-chain corruption repair-tail MUST refuse
after a successful append the bytes are durably on disk (fsync) before return
clauses.reason: durability is not observable from outside the process (the reference fixture treats R-8 as static)

clauses.clause: exit 0 on success
exit 2 on a usage error
exit 3 on an I/O error
exit 4 on a conflict
clauses.reason: as R-4.3/3 (OD-BATCH)

clauses.clause: exit 5 on corruption (verify not ok, repair-tail non-tail corruption)
stdlib only; the allowed modules
use `from __future__ import annotations`
no pip install of a runtime dependency
clauses.reason: an installation practice; its product consequence is R-10/1

clauses.clause: Python 3.11+ required
clauses.reason: a property of the runtime environment the harness chooses, not of the product's behaviour

clauses.clause: unit tests, >=85% coverage, unittest/pytest agreement
clauses.reason: DEVELOPER_TEST_REQUIREMENT: a requirement on the product's own tests, outside ProductProof by invariant IX; not satisfied by this classification

clauses.clause: no socket, no subprocess, no os.system
no opening of files outside the ledger, batch and snapshot paths
clauses.reason: no class observes which files a subject opens

clauses.clause: ledgerlock/__init__.py, ledger.py, cli.py
ledger.py: Ledger, ConflictError, append, verify, snapshot, apply_batch
tests/test_*.py, docs/requirements.md, README.md, pyproject.toml
clauses.reason: repository deliverables: the developer's tests (R-11) and packaging/documentation files, not product behaviour; the reference fixture carries the package tree only

clauses.reason: a summary of R-3..R-12: item 1 S-9-a, 2 S-6-d, 3 R-5/4 (unsupported, OD-BATCH), 4 S-7-a, 5 R-11 (engineering), 6 S-10-a
